title: Solving proportions by cross-multiplication
blurb: Set up a proportion with matching units in matching places, solve it by cross-multiplying, and spot when a relationship is inverse instead.
question: Carlos's car uses 4 gallons of gas to drive 126 miles. His clinical rotation is 441 miles round trip. The HESI A2 asks how many gallons he needs, and, separately, how long 3 nurses take to do a job that takes 4 nurses 6 hours. Which one is a simple proportion, and how do you set each up?

teach.body: Formally, a proportion is an equation stating that two ratios are equal: a/b = c/d. In plain English: the same relationship at a different size. If 4 gallons take you 126 miles, then 8 gallons take you 252 miles; the ratio of gallons to miles stays the same. When one value is missing, a proportion lets you find it in one line, which is why it is one of the most useful tools on the HESI A2 Math exam.

In a/b = c/d, the cross products are equal: a × d = b × c. This works because multiplying both sides by b and by d clears both denominators. So for 3/x = 12/20: 12 × x = 3 × 20, giving 12x = 60 and x = 5. The calculator route is always the same: multiply the two numbers on the diagonal that has no x, then divide by the number on the diagonal with the x.

steps.label: Say it in words
steps.sub: gallons per miles = gallons per miles

steps.label: Match the units
steps.sub: Same units on top, same units below

items: Shortcut when it is obvious: 63 is 7 × 9, so x = 4 × 9 = 36. Both routes agree.
Map scales are proportions too: 1 in = 25 mi, so 1/25 = 3.5/x gives x = 87.5 miles. When the drawing side is not 1 (2 cm = 15 km), the proportion handles it: 2/15 = 9.4/x, so x = 70.5 km.

teach.h: 3 cups of flour make 24 cookies. Flour for 60 cookies?
teach.caption: Sense-check: 60 cookies is 2.5 times 24, so the flour should be 2.5 × 3 = 7.5 cups. 480 cups is absurd.

teach.text: Two set-up slips create most proportion distractors: putting the second ratio upside down (3/24 = 60/x), and mixing units inside a ratio (inches on one side, feet on the other). Convert to one unit first and write the unit labels next to every number. Also watch for 'additive thinking': 4 to 6 is not the same as 24 to 26.

items: Carlos's car uses 4 gallons for 126 miles. How many gallons for 441 miles? Let x = gallons.
Gallons over miles on both sides: 4/126 = x/441.
Check: 441 ÷ 126 = 3.5 times the distance, and 3.5 × 4 = 14 gallons. ✓

teach.caption: Direct: gallons and miles, cost and quantity. Inverse: workers and time for one job, speed and time for a fixed distance.

items: 4 nurses take 6 hours to finish an inventory. How long would 3 nurses take at the same rate?
Fewer nurses means MORE time, so it is inverse. Total work: 4 × 6 = 24 nurse-hours.
Time for 3 nurses: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 hours. Check: 3 × 8 = 24. ✓ (A direct proportion would give 4.5 hours, the wrong direction.)
A trip takes 3 hours at 60 mph. At 45 mph: distance = 180 miles, and 180 ÷ 45 = 4 hours. Check: 60 × 3 = 45 × 4 = 180. ✓

teach.caption: Similar figures have corresponding sides in the same ratio. Match height with height and shadow with shadow.

items: A proportion is two equal ratios: a/b = c/d, so a × d = b × c.
Keep the same units in the same positions; convert units before you start.
Calculator route: multiply the diagonal without x, divide by the number with x.
Direct: both grow together (ratios equal). Inverse: one grows as the other shrinks (products equal).
Sense-check the direction and size of every answer.

summary: You can now set up a proportion with matching units in matching positions, solve it by cross-multiplying and sense-check the result. You can also recognize inverse relationships such as workers and time, and use proportions with similar figures and shadows.

whyNot.0: 115.2 multiplies 72 by 8/5, the ratio turned upside down.
whyNot.2: 69 uses additive thinking: 8 − 5 = 3, so 72 − 3. Proportions scale by multiplying.

A.q: A nurse walks 2.4 km during a 30-minute break. At the same pace, how far would she walk in 75 minutes?
A.why: 2.4/30 = x/75. Cross-multiply: 30x = 2.4 × 75 = 180. Divide: x = 6 km. Check: 75 minutes is 2.5 times 30, and 2.5 × 2.4 = 6. ✓

whyNot.1: 0.96 km sets up the second ratio upside down (2.4 × 30 ÷ 75), giving less distance for more time.
whyNot.3: 47.4 km adds the extra 45 minutes to the 2.4 km, mixing minutes with kilometers.

A.q: Four nurses take 6 hours to complete a supply inventory. Working at the same rate, how long would 3 nurses take?
A.why: Fewer workers take longer, so this is inverse. Total work: 4 × 6 = 24 nurse-hours. 24 ÷ 3 = 8 hours.

whyNot.0: 4.5 hours treats the relationship as direct (6 × 3/4), so fewer nurses would finish faster.
whyNot.1: 5 hours subtracts one hour for one fewer nurse; time does not change by fixed steps.
whyNot.3: 7 hours adds one hour for one fewer nurse; the total work is 24 nurse-hours, so the time is 24 ÷ 3.

B.q: A photo 4 inches wide and 6 inches tall is enlarged proportionally so that its width is 2 feet. What is the new height?
B.why: Convert first: 2 ft = 24 in. 4/6 = 24/x, so 4x = 144 and x = 36 in (3 ft). Check: 24 is 6 times 4, and 6 × 6 = 36. ✓

whyNot.0: 3 in mixes units: 4/6 = 2/x uses feet on one side and inches on the other.
whyNot.1: 16 in sets up width over height on one side and height over width on the other (4/6 = x/24).
whyNot.3: 26 in adds the 20-inch increase in width to the height instead of scaling it.

B.why: Cross-multiply: 9(x − 1) = 6 × 12 = 72. Divide: x − 1 = 8. Add 1: x = 9. Check: 6/8 = 0.75 and 9/12 = 0.75. ✓

whyNot.0: 8 is the value of x − 1, one step short of x.
whyNot.1: 7 subtracts 1 from 8 instead of adding it.
whyNot.2: 5.5 flips the first ratio: (x − 1)/6 = 9/12 gives x − 1 = 4.5.

B.q: A 5-ft-tall student casts a 3-ft shadow. At the same time, a light pole casts a 12-ft shadow. How tall is the light pole?
B.why: Height over shadow: 5/3 = x/12. Cross-multiply: 3x = 60. Divide: x = 20 ft. Check: 12 is 4 times 3, and 4 × 5 = 20. ✓

whyNot.0: 7.2 ft flips one ratio (3/5 × 12), which would make the pole shorter than its shadow.
whyNot.2: 14 ft adds the 2-ft difference between height and shadow; similar figures scale by multiplying.
whyNot.3: 60 ft is the cross product 3x, one step short of x.

C.q: A hospital shuttle's trip takes 50 minutes at an average speed of 36 mph. How long would the same trip take at an average speed of 40 mph?
C.why: Same distance, so speed × time is constant: 36 × 50 = 40 × t, so t = 1,800 ÷ 40 = 45 minutes. Check: the distance is 36 × 50/60 = 30 miles, and 30 ÷ 40 = 0.75 h = 45 min. ✓

whyNot.0: 55.6 min treats speed and time as direct (50 × 40/36), so the faster shuttle would take longer.
whyNot.1: 46 min subtracts the 4-mph increase from the time; inverse proportions scale by multiplying.
whyNot.2: 30 is the distance in miles, not a time in minutes.

C.q: Which pair of quantities is in an inverse proportion?
options: Number of pumps and time to fill a pool
Gallons of gas bought and total cost
Miles driven and time at a steady speed
Doses given and total milligrams used
C.why: Doubling the pumps halves the time to fill the same pool: as one grows, the other shrinks, with a constant product.

whyNot.1: More gallons cost more at a fixed price: a direct proportion.
whyNot.2: At a steady speed, more time means more miles: a direct proportion.
whyNot.3: More doses of the same strength use more milligrams: a direct proportion.

C.q: A unit staffs 2 nurses for every 9 patients. The unit has 36 patients, and then 9 more are admitted. How many ADDITIONAL nurses are needed to keep the same ratio?
C.why: 36 patients: 2/9 = x/36, so x = 8 nurses. 45 patients: 2/9 = y/45, so y = 10 nurses. Additional: 10 − 8 = 2. (Or: 9 more patients is one more group of 9, so 2 more nurses.)

whyNot.0: 10 is the total number of nurses needed for 45 patients, not the additional number.
whyNot.1: 40.5 flips the second ratio (2/9 = 9/x), giving patients where nurses belong.
whyNot.2: 1 assumes one nurse per 9 patients; the ratio is 2 nurses per 9 patients.

reteach.title: Zooming a photo on your phone
reteach.question: When you pinch-zoom a photo, everything gets bigger together and nothing gets stretched. How is that the same as a proportion?

blocks.body: Zooming multiplies every length by the same factor. If the photo's width goes from 4 to 24 (× 6), its height must also be multiplied by 6, so 6 becomes 36. If you ADDED 20 to both instead, the picture would look squashed. A proportion is just the statement 'the same multiplier on both': 4/6 = 24/36. Cross-multiplying finds the missing length without having to spot the multiplier.

blocks.h: Width and height, before and after a × 6 zoom

blocks.text: A zoom never adds the same amount to each side; it multiplies. 'Width up by 20, so height up by 20' is additive thinking, and it gives a distorted picture and a wrong answer.

explain.body: In a/b = c/d, a × d = b × c. Multiply the diagonal without x, then divide by the number on the diagonal with x.

test.q: Solve for x: 7/x = 21/36. Round to the nearest tenth if needed.

explain.body: Write the ratio in words first, such as pens over dollars, and keep that order on both sides. Same units on top, same units on the bottom.

test.q: Four pens cost $6. Which proportion correctly finds the cost, c, of 15 pens?
test.why: Pens over dollars on both sides: 4/6 = 15/c. Cross-multiply: 4c = 90, so c = $22.50.

whyNot.0: 4/6 = c/15 puts dollars on top of the second ratio, so the units do not match.
whyNot.1: 6/4 = 15/c has dollars over pens on the left but pens over dollars on the right.
whyNot.3: 4/15 compares old pens with new pens, so the right side must be old cost over new cost (6/c), not c/6.

explain.body: When one quantity rises as the other falls (workers and time, speed and time), the PRODUCT stays the same. Find the total, then divide.

test.q: Six volunteers can pack the clinic's supply kits in 5 hours. At the same rate, how long would 10 volunteers take?
test.why: Total work: 6 × 5 = 30 volunteer-hours. With 10 volunteers: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 hours.

whyNot.0: 8.3 hours treats it as direct (5 × 10/6), so more volunteers would take longer.
whyNot.2: 1 hour subtracts one hour per extra volunteer; inverse relationships scale by dividing.
whyNot.3: 9 hours adds time for extra volunteers, the wrong direction.

explain.body: Similar shapes have equal angles and proportional sides. Pair each side with the side in the same position on the other shape.

test.q: Two triangles are similar. The small one has a short side of 4 cm and a long side of 7 cm. The large one's short side is 10 cm. How long is its long side?
test.why: 4/7 = 10/x. Cross-multiply: 4x = 70. Divide: x = 17.5 cm. Check: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, and 7 × 2.5 = 17.5. ✓

whyNot.0: 13 cm adds the 6-cm difference in short sides; similar figures scale by multiplying.
whyNot.1: 2.8 cm flips one ratio (10/4 = 7/x), making the large triangle's long side smaller.
whyNot.3: 70 is the cross product 4x, one step short of x.
